raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

NVFP4 BERT, RoBERTa and XLM-R write the FFN's bias add + GELU output in 16 bits and read it back to quantize it for the down projection. This PR fuses the three into one kernel, called from BERT's FFN through the manual act+quant fusion (`maybe_fused_act_quant`, #51415). Follows #61755.

## Claims

- New op `gelu_nvfp4_quant`: NVFP4 of `gelu(input + bias)` computed in fp32 with one rounding, in `scaled_fp4_quant`'s layout. It shares a templated kernel with `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant`, whose output is unchanged.
- BERT hands the up projection's bias to the kernel only when the down projection takes NVFP4 input, so FP16 and FP8 are unchanged.
- `BAAI/bge-reranker-v2-m3` NVFP4 on an RTX PRO 6000: 16-20% less GPU time, now 17-23% below FP8, with unchanged ranking quality.

## Validation

RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), torch 2.14.0, FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1, main 34d5de18.

- `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_gelu_nvfp4_quant.py tests/kernels/quantization/test_silu_mul_nvfp4_quant.py tests/compile/passes/test_silu_mul_quant_manual_fusion.py`: 108 passed.
- `silu_and_mul_nvfp4_quant`: identical bytes to main (20 cases).
- `gelu_nvfp4_quant` vs `scaled_fp4_quant` of the fp32 reference: 1 of 68M bytes differs.
- Unfused fallback (`requires_unquantized_input` on the down projection, as under LoRA): scores identical to main.

GPU kernel time of one `classify` call on 128 sequences (ModelOpt `NVFP4_DEFAULT_CFG`, `LLM(runner="pooling", dtype="float16")`, mean of 3 runs, 2 for FP8, spread < 1.3%):

| Tokens/seq | FP8 | NVFP4, main | NVFP4, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 160 | 27.8 ms | 27.7 ms | 22.3 ms (-19.5%) |
| 320 | 65.1 ms | 60.2 ms | 49.8 ms (-17.3%) |
| 640 | 137.1 ms | 134.6 ms | 113.5 ms (-15.7%) |

Recall@10 vs PyTorch FP32 on all 741 questions (Ko-StrategyQA / MIRACL-ko): 0.879 / 0.929 on main, 0.873 / 0.931 with this PR. Scores differ slightly from main because Inductor's bias + GELU rounds differently in about 1% of fp16 values.

## Details

- **Bias:** BERT sets `skip_bias_add` on the up projection when the down projection exposes the NVFP4 input key. If no fused kernel applies at run time (e.g. LoRA on the down projection), `maybe_fused_act_quant` adds the bias itself. With LoRA on the up projection, the bias now comes after the LoRA delta.
- **Duplicates:** no open PR fuses exact GELU into NVFP4 quant. #59467 (GELU-tanh x mul) templates the same kernel the same way, so whichever lands second rebases.
- **CI:** the kernel test is added to `(B200) Kernels`; the fusion test already runs in `(B200) Fusion and Compile`. Validated at TP=1 only.
- **AI assistance:** prepared with Claude Code (kernel, wiring, tests, validation, this text). I reviewed every changed line and the results.

---

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from tests.kernels.quantization.nvfp4_utils import (
+    FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX,
+    FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX,
+    convert_swizzled_to_linear,
+    dequantize_nvfp4_to_dtype,
+)
+from vllm._custom_ops import scaled_fp4_quant
+from vllm.platforms import current_platform
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import round_up
+from vllm.utils.torch_utils import set_random_seed
+
+if not current_platform.has_device_capability(100):
+    pytest.skip(
+        reason="Nvfp4 Requires compute capability of 10 or above.",
+        allow_module_level=True,
+    )
+
+DTYPES = [torch.float16, torch.bfloat16]
+# (M, K). K = 48, 80 and 3696 are 16 mod 32, so the NVFP4 linear pads K. M not a
+# multiple of 128 or K not a multiple of 64 leaves padding in the 128x4 scale tiles.
+SHAPES = [
+    (128, 128),
+    (256, 64),
+    (1, 128),
+    (64, 4096),
+    (5, 48),
+    (130, 80),
+    (130, 96),
+    (2, 3696),
+]
+BLOCK_SIZE = 16
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", DTYPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("shape", SHAPES)
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("has_bias", [True, False])
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def test_gelu_nvfp4_quant(
+    default_vllm_config,
+    dtype: torch.dtype,
+    shape: tuple[int, int],
+    has_bias: bool,
+) -> None:
+    set_random_seed(42)
+    device = "cuda:0"
+    torch.set_default_device(device)
+
+    m, k = shape
+    x = torch.randn(shape, dtype=dtype)
+    bias = torch.randn(k, dtype=dtype) if has_bias else None
+
+    # ref op, computed in fp32 and rounded once like the kernel, and quantized into
+    # the K-padded buffer that the CUTLASS NVFP4 linear uses
+    ref_input = x.float() if bias is None else x.float() + bias.float()
+    ref_output = torch.nn.functional.gelu(ref_input).to(dtype)
+    ref_global_scale = (FLOAT8_E4M3_MAX * FLOAT4_E2M1_MAX) / torch.abs(
+        ref_output
+    ).max().to(torch.float32)
+    ref_output_quant, ref_block_scale = scaled_fp4_quant(
+        ref_output, ref_global_scale, padded_n=round_up(k, 32)
+    )
+
+    # fused op, into buffers holding stale bytes as under torch.compile buffer reuse
+    fused_output_quant = torch.full_like(ref_output_quant, 0xFF)
+    fused_block_scale = torch.empty_like(ref_block_scale)
+    fused_block_scale.view(torch.uint8).fill_(0xFF)
+    torch.ops._C.gelu_nvfp4_quant(
+        fused_output_quant, fused_block_scale, x, ref_global_scale, bias
+    )
+
+    # check padding: zero data beyond K, zero scales outside the [M, K / 16] block
+    assert not fused_output_quant[:, k // 2 :].any()
+    sf_rows, sf_cols = fused_block_scale.shape
+    fused_sf = convert_swizzled_to_linear(
+        fused_block_scale.view(torch.uint8), sf_rows, sf_cols * BLOCK_SIZE, BLOCK_SIZE
+    )
+    outside = torch.ones_like(fused_sf, dtype=torch.bool)
+    outside[:m, : k // BLOCK_SIZE] = False
+    assert not fused_sf[outside].any()
+
+    # check dequantized output
+    ref_output_dequant = dequantize_nvfp4_to_dtype(
+        ref_output_quant, ref_block_scale, ref_global_scale, dtype, device
+    )
+    fused_output_dequant = dequantize_nvfp4_to_dtype(
+        fused_output_quant, fused_block_scale, ref_global_scale, dtype, device
+    )
+    torch.testing.assert_close(
+        ref_output_dequant, fused_output_dequant, atol=3e-1, rtol=3e-1
+    )
